visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A male presenter with dark, styled hair wears a white t-shirt while standing against a neutral grey wall. He holds a rectangular makeup palette with an integrated mirror, pointing his finger toward a specific pan of brown eyeshadow that has visible cracks and damage. (2) The camera provides a close-up shot of the eyeshadow palette, revealing ten different square pans of varied brown and neutral shades. One pan in the bottom row is significantly shattered, with loose powder spilling across the interior surface of the reflective container. (3) The man holds a thin metal spatula tool and uses it to scrape and crush the remaining fragments of broken eyeshadow within the metal pan. He performs this action carefully to demonstrate the traditional method of grinding the product back into a fine powder state. (4) He covers the crushed eyeshadow pan with a small piece of white paper or tissue and applies firm pressure with his thumb to compress the powder. This is shown as part of a demonstration of a popular but discouraged DIY repair technique. (5) The presenter gestures toward his face and eyes while speaking directly to the viewer about the risks of bacteria. He holds the palette and the metal tool, emphasizing that domestic environments lack the sterile conditions of professional manufacturing cleanrooms and labs. (6) In the final segment, he smiles and gives a thumbs-up gesture while holding the palette. He concludes the video by advising viewers to prioritize eye health and beauty by replacing the damaged product rather than attempting unhygienic repairs with alcohol and tools.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) A friendly male voice asks a question about broken eyeshadow in Mandarin, accompanied by a bright, mid-tempo acoustic pop background track. The music features light guitar strumming and a steady, rhythmic beat that sets an energetic and helpful instructional tone. (2) The speaker introduces himself as Kai Mi and promises to share the correct way to handle damaged makeup. The BGM continues at a consistent volume, while his speech rate is moderate and his tone remains animated and engaging for the audience. (3) As he shows the broken palette, a metallic clink sound occurs from the palette being handled. He jokes that the best solution is to 'buy a new one,' followed by a brief, playful pause in his narration before explaining he is kidding. (4) A distinct gritty, scraping sound is heard as a metal tool grinds the eyeshadow powder. This is followed by the soft rustle of paper being pressed and a short, airy hiss from a spray bottle, representing the application of alcohol. (5) His voice takes on a more professional and cautionary tone as he explains the lack of a 'cleanroom' environment at home. He mentions dust and bacteria in a lower pitch, emphasizing the serious health risks associated with contaminated eye products. (6) The video ends with his voice returning to a bright, encouraging pitch. He reiterates the suggestion to buy a new palette for health and beauty. The background music swells slightly before fading out as he finishes his final sentence and advice.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Linear: Hook -> Myth-busting -> Health Advice -> Conclusion
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to discourage makeup users from attempting to DIY repair shattered eyeshadow palettes. By debunking common online 'fix' hacks using alcohol and pressing, the creator highlights the risks of bacterial contamination and loss of product integrity due to unsterile domestic conditions, ultimately advising viewers to replace damaged products for eye safety.

high_inference.freeDescribe: The video uses a humorous bait-and-switch at the beginning to grab attention before delivering serious health-related advice regarding cosmetic hygiene.
